findings.title: A killed/crashed ingest_archive process leaves the job stuck non-terminal forever; nothing times it out
findings.suggested_fix: The command's own docstring claims 'every exit path writes a terminal status, including the unexpected ones,' but that is only true for exceptions Python can catch. A SIGKILL (OOM killer, container eviction, `kill -9`) or a hard segfault in a native dependency (duckdb/pandas/gdal) skips the except/finally in handle() (controllers.py's write_status(state=RUNNING,...) at startUpload/uploadRun is the last thing written) and the job status object is never updated to FAILED. Nothing else in the system watches the job: _launch() in controllers.py is fire-and-forget with no supervisor, and uploadStatus() just echoes back whatever is in storage. The client in ngiab-upload-run.js polls `for (;;)` with no ceiling (see finding on that file), so the UI shows 'Working…' indefinitely with no way for the user to tell a hung job from a genuinely slow 8,000-catchment conversion. Add a watchdog: either have uploadStatus() treat a RUNNING status whose `updated` timestamp is older than a generous ceiling (e.g. 2x the longest observed conversion) as failed, or have the poll loop itself give up and report 'still running past the expected time, check server logs' after N minutes.

findings.title: subprocess.Popen failure (e.g. django-admin missing) leaves the job status stuck at pending/queued and orphans the staged archive with no cleanup
findings.suggested_fix: startUpload (line 386) and uploadRun (line 414) call _launch() with no try/except. _launch's subprocess.Popen (line 457) resolves the executable from `os.path.dirname(sys.executable)`; if `django-admin` is not there (a stripped/slim environment, PATH surprises inside a container rebuild) Popen raises FileNotFoundError synchronously, before the request returns. That propagates out of the uncaught view as a 500. By then write_status(state=PENDING, stage='queued', ...) has already been written (line 384/412), and for the presigned-upload path the archive bytes are already sitting in storage at ingest.staging_key(job_id) -- nothing ever runs discard_staged() for a job that never launched, so the archive and its status object are permanently orphaned under `_uploads/<job>/`. Wrap the Popen call in try/except, write a FAILED status and best-effort discard_staged(job_id) on launch failure, and return a clean error to the caller instead of a bare 500.

findings.title: uploadStatus does not catch StorageUnreachable, so a single transient storage hiccup permanently aborts client polling for a job that may still succeed
findings.suggested_fix: ingest.read_status() (ingest.py:98-115) re-raises any exception from backend.exists()/backend.open() as run_store.StorageUnreachable. uploadStatus() (controllers.py:418-429) does not catch it, so a transient S3 blip during polling (a read timeout, a 500 from the object store, a brief network partition) turns into an uncaught exception and a 500 response. The client's poll loop in ngiab-upload-run.js (_await, lines 106-135) treats any error from appAPI.uploadStatus as fatal: it calls this._busy(false) and reports the error, permanently stopping the loop -- even though the background ingest_archive process is still running and may finish successfully. The user is told the upload failed when it did not. Catch StorageUnreachable in uploadStatus and answer with a retryable signal (e.g. 503 with terminal:false, or the last known non-terminal status) so a transient read failure does not end the poll; correspondingly the client should retry a status-check failure a few times before giving up rather than aborting on the first error.

findings.title: Client poll loop has no timeout or maximum-attempt ceiling
findings.suggested_fix: _await(job) is `for (;;)` with a 2s sleep and no cap on iterations or elapsed time (lines 106-135). Combined with the server-side gap where a killed job never reaches a terminal state (see the ingest_archive.py finding), this means the browser tab can poll every 2 seconds indefinitely with no feedback beyond 'Working…', and no way for the user to abandon the wait short of reloading the page. There is also no AbortController/disconnectedCallback to stop the loop if the element is ever removed from the DOM in the future. Add an elapsed-time or attempt-count ceiling that surfaces 'this is taking longer than expected, check back later' and stops polling, and wire an AbortController into the fetch so a future disconnectedCallback can cancel in-flight polling.

findings.title: Launched subprocess is never reaped (no wait()/poll()/SIGCHLD handling), accumulating zombie processes
findings.suggested_fix: _launch() creates the Popen object, discards the reference, and never calls .wait()/.poll() on it; nothing else in the codebase calls waitpid or installs a SIGCHLD handler. On Linux, a child that exits becomes a zombie until its parent reaps it, so every completed upload leaves a defunct process entry until the uvicorn worker process itself exits/restarts. Under sustained upload traffic this accumulates entries in the process table (bounded by ulimit -u / pid_max), which is a slow resource leak rather than an immediate outage, but is easy to fix: register a SIGCHLD handler that reaps with a non-blocking waitpid loop, or periodically poll a small registry of outstanding Popen handles.

findings.title: No bound on concurrent ingest subprocesses launched per upload request
findings.suggested_fix: startUpload and uploadRun launch a new ingest_archive subprocess (via _launch) with no semaphore, queue, or count check anywhere in controllers.py or ingest.py. The ingest.py module docstring itself notes conversion of a large run 'holds the GIL through DuckDB and pandas' long enough to matter, and the portal serves on a single uvicorn worker (ASGI_PROCESSES=1) by design. Two or more authorized users (or one user double-clicking Upload) starting large conversions at the same time will run that many concurrent DuckDB/pandas processes on the same host with no coordination, competing for memory and CPU with no ceiling. Given uploads are gated by UPLOAD_PERMISSION this is a lower-likelihood path, but it is unguarded in code today. Consider a small in-storage or in-process semaphore that queues or rejects a new ingest while N are already running.

residual_risks: No explicit connect/read timeouts or retry policy are set for the S3-backed run_store or duckdb_conn paths in this diff; behavior falls back to django-storages/boto3 and DuckDB httpfs defaults, which this review could not verify from the diff alone (moderate-to-low confidence, suppressed as a finding).

The Dockerfile and apptainer/ngiab.def carry no HEALTHCHECK, but this predates this diff (verified against the pre-diff Dockerfile) and the app is deployed into an existing Tethys portal whose own orchestration/health-checking is outside this diff's scope -- not re-flagged as a new gap.

archive.extract() and the ingest workspace (tempfile.mkdtemp in ingest.publish) were read but not deeply audited for disk-space exhaustion or decompression-bomb behavior; out of the reviewer's FOCUS list for this pass.
testing_gaps: No test appears to cover a job whose status object is left stuck at RUNNING (simulating a SIGKILLed ingest_archive process) and what uploadStatus / the client poll loop do with it.
No test appears to cover _launch()/Popen failure (missing executable) and whether the staged archive and status object it orphans are ever cleaned up.
No test appears to cover uploadStatus's behavior when read_status raises StorageUnreachable mid-poll.
